notes.key_messages: Candidates need to be able to apply their understanding of concepts on the syllabus to unfamiliar examples, such as in Question 2(b)(iii), which required application of understanding of cell signalling to the unfamiliar signalling molecule ghrelin. Similarly, Question 4(c) required application of understanding of the cardiac cycle to the unfamiliar heart condition, cardiac tamponade. Candidates who have the opportunity to practise these skills throughout the course will benefit when tackling exam questions such as these. Candidates should be able to analyse data and suggest biological explanations for the patterns they see.
